t: Faith That Doesn’t Give Up
v: Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
Behold, a Canaanite woman came out from that region and cried, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely demon-possessed.”
But he answered her not a word. His disciples came and begged him, saying, “Send her away, for she cries after us.”
But he answered, “I was not sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
But she came and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
But he answered, “It is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
b: This passage shows us a mother’s faith that would not give up. She came to Jesus because her daughter was suffering, and even though she was a Gentile, she cried out for the Lord’s mercy. Faith often begins in pain. When people come to the end of the road, they seek the Lord more deeply.

Jesus was silent at first, and then seemed to refuse her, yet the woman did not step back. She was not defeated by her circumstances, and she was not tripped up by his words. Instead she bowed down even more humbly and said, “Lord, help me.” True faith is not emotional excitement. It is holding on to the Lord even when there seems to be no answer.

The woman said that even the crumbs were enough for her. She knew that even a little of the Lord’s grace is enough to turn a life around. Jesus praised her: “Great is your faith!” Great faith is not loud faith; it is faith that endures to the end. It does not ask for glory for itself, but trusts only in the Lord’s mercy and power.
a: Come to the Lord even in hardship
Do not stay away from Jesus because the problem seems too big.
Keep believing in the silence
Even when you cannot yet see a response, do not stop praying.
Hold on to grace with humility
Admit your limits and believe that the Lord’s grace is enough.
q: When God seems silent, do I give up, or do I keep holding on to him tightly?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me faith like the Canaanite woman’s, a faith that does not give up. When I pray and have not yet seen the answer, help me still to believe in Your mercy and power. Let me keep coming to You in difficulty until I see Your fulfillment. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not give up seeking the Lord. My faith endures to the end, and the Lord will accomplish his good purpose.

t: A Life That Overcomes Evil with Good
v: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil. Cling to that which is good.
In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor preferring one another;
not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
rejoicing in hope; enduring in troubles; continuing steadfastly in prayer;
contributing to the needs of the saints; given to hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.
Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God’s wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”
Therefore “if your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head.”
Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
b: This passage paints a picture of the Christian life: love must be genuine, not pretended. True love is not polite words on the lips. It hates evil, clings to good, and is willing to pay a price for others. When Christ lives within, love is no longer a performance but the natural overflow of life.

Paul especially points out that we are to endure in troubles and continue steadfastly in prayer. This shows that a life belonging to God is not free of pressure, but holds on to hope in the midst of it. People who rely on themselves quickly grow cold and weary, but by the Holy Spirit we can be fervent in spirit and keep serving the Lord.

The greatest challenge is this: “Repay no one evil for evil, but overcome evil with good.” The world’s logic is revenge; the Kingdom’s logic is victory. When we are hurt and still choose to bless, when we are wronged and still choose to be kind, that is not weakness. It is the life of Christ made visible. True victory is not defeating others, but overcoming the evil within ourselves.
a: Live out genuine love
Let love come from the heart, not just surface courtesy.
Stay fervent in hardship
Overcome weariness with prayer and hope.
Answer evil with good
Refuse revenge; choose blessing and kindness.
q: When I am offended, do I respond in the world’s way, or with the life of Christ?
pr: Heavenly Father, place genuine love within me, so that I hate what is evil and cling to what is good. When I am hurt, help me not to repay evil for evil, but to overcome evil with good. Let Jesus live out his victorious life in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not be overcome by evil. By the life of Christ, I overcome evil with good.

t: The Light Has Come: New Life for Those Who Receive Him
v: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.
The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.
He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.
The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.
He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.
But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:
who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
b: This passage declares who Jesus is: he is the Word who was in the beginning, the God who was with God. All things were made through him, and life is in him. This means Jesus is not merely a figure in history. He is the Creator, the source of life, and the true answer for every person.

The text says, “The life was the light of men.” Apart from God, people live in darkness: lost, afraid, self-centered, bound by sin. But Jesus is the true light. He came not to condemn but to shine. When the light comes, the darkness is exposed; when the light comes, the road becomes clear; when the light comes, life has hope.

Most precious of all: “As many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children.” Believing in Jesus is not just a religious choice; it is a change of identity. From sinner to child, from an orphan’s heart to a heart at home in the Father’s house, from the old life into new life. The Word became flesh so that we could draw near to God, and so that Christ could live in us.
a: Receive Jesus as Lord of your life
Not just knowing about him, but truly letting him come in and reign.
Let the true light shine into your heart
Give your darkness, wounds, and sin to the Lord for healing.
Live as a child of God
No longer live in fear, but in the Father’s love.
q: Do I only know about Jesus, or have I truly received him as Lord of my life?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus into the world to be my light and my life. Shine into the darkness of my heart, so that I may truly receive Jesus and live out my identity as Your child. Let me walk in grace and truth every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is the true light. I receive him. I am a child of God, living in new life.

t: A Small Lapse Can Lead to a Great Fall
v: At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.
At evening, David arose from his bed, and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful to look at.
David sent and inquired after the woman. One said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”
David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.
The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “I am with child.”
b: This passage records a major turning point in David’s life. The text points out the problem right at the start: “At the time when kings go out… David stayed at Jerusalem.” The one who should have been at the front stayed in a place of comfort. Many falls do not happen suddenly; they begin when we are out of our proper place.

Next David saw, inquired, sent, and took. Sin often develops step by step: the eyes linger, the heart stirs, and action follows. If we are not alert in small things, selfish desire grows. Satan does not always strike people down with something big; often he slowly opens a crack through small lapses.

David was a man after God’s own heart, yet he still fell. This reminds us that spiritual experience cannot replace daily watchfulness. True safety is not found in past victories, but in whether we let Jesus be King today. When we depend on the Holy Spirit wholeheartedly, we are guarded; when we relax and depend on ourselves, we easily lose ground.
a: Stay in the place God gave you
Be faithful where you are responsible; do not run from your calling.
Be alert in small things
Watch your eyes, your thoughts, and your daily habits.
Let the Lord be King every day
Do not live on yesterday’s grace; depend on the Lord today.
q: Is there a lapse in my life that seems small but is slowly bringing danger?
pr: Heavenly Father, guard my heart so that I do not grow slack in comfort or self-confident in success. Help me stay alert in small things and let Jesus be King in me every day. Keep me far from temptation and walking in holiness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I stay alert and keep watch. I stand in the place God gave me, let the Lord be King, and stay far from falling.

t: Treasure in Jars of Clay
v: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves.
We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
always carrying around in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
So then death works in us, but life in you.
b: This passage first points out a truth: we are clay jars. Clay jars are plain, fragile, and easily broken, representing human limitation and weakness. Yet God put a treasure inside a clay jar. That treasure is the life of Christ and the power of the gospel. God arranged it this way on purpose, so that people would know the power is not from us but from God.

So Paul says that though we are pressed on every side, we are not crushed; though struck down, we are not destroyed. There may be pressure outside, but there is treasure inside; circumstances may attack, but life has power. When we admit we are clay jars, we are better able to experience God’s power.

“Carrying around the putting to death of Jesus, that the life of Jesus may be revealed.” This is the way of the cross. When the old self is dealt with and self is laid down, the life of Christ shines out. Selflessness is not loss; it is letting Jesus live through us. If the clay jar is willing to be broken, the glory of the treasure can shine through.
a: Accept your limits
Do not rely on your own strength; admit that you need God.
Trust the Lord under pressure
Though circumstances are hard, God’s power is still at work within.
Be willing to let the old self die
Lay yourself down so that the life of Christ may be revealed.
q: Am I hiding my weakness, or letting God’s great power be shown in my weakness?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for placing Your precious life in this clay jar of mine. When I am weak, let me experience Your power more deeply. Help me lay down myself so that the life of Jesus may be revealed in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am a clay jar, and Christ is the treasure. God’s great power is fully revealed in my weakness.

t: Only the Word of God Stands Forever
v: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
“Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of Yahweh in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.
Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low. The crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places a plain.
The glory of Yahweh shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it.”
The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, because Yahweh’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
b: This passage begins with “comfort.” God speaks to a people who are wounded, exiled, and worn out from the battle: be comforted. This shows that God is not only a God of judgment, but also a God full of mercy and restoration. When people repent and turn back, God declares forgiveness and a new beginning.

Then God says to prepare the way in the wilderness. The wilderness stands for desolation, dryness, and difficulty, yet God can open a road in the wilderness and make a highway in the desert. The uneven ground will be made level, and the rough places a plain. This means God can change circumstances we cannot change, and straighten lives that have become crooked.

Finally, God contrasts the brevity of people with the permanence of his word. People are like grass, and their beauty like a flower; they quickly fade. The voices of the world also pass in a moment. But “the word of our God stands forever.” When circumstances shake, holding on to God’s word gives us a foundation. Human words change; God’s word does not.
a: Receive God’s comfort
Bring your weariness and burdens to the Lord.
Believe God can make a way
Keep expecting God to act even in the wilderness.
Hold on to the eternal word
Let the Bible be the foundation of your life.
q: When the world shifts, am I holding on to the voices of people, or to God’s unchanging word?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who comforts me. When I walk through the wilderness, open a way for me and make the road ahead level. Help me hold fast to Your word, so that I stand firm even in turbulent times. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of God stands forever. I will stand firm.

t: A Worker Who Has No Need to Be Ashamed
v: Remind them of these things, charging them in the sight of the Lord that they not argue about words, to no profit, to the subverting of those who hear.
Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the word of truth.
But shun empty chatter, for it will proceed further in ungodliness,
and their word will eat like gangrene, of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus,
men who have erred concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past, and overthrowing the faith of some.
However the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are his,” and, “Let every one who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness.”
Flee from youthful lusts, and follow after righteousness, faith, love, and peace, with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
But refuse foolish and ignorant questionings, knowing that they generate strife.
The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient,
b: This passage reminds us that people who belong to God should not spend their lives on pointless arguments. Fighting over words may seem reasonable, but it can ruin those who listen. The purpose of truth is not to win debates but to build up lives. When the focus moves from Jesus to winning and losing, we have left the path.

Paul says to be “a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the word of truth.” This means taking God’s word seriously: not twisting it, not interpreting it by our own ideas, but teaching it faithfully and honestly. To be truly approved by God is not about outward reputation, but about being faithful before God.

Then Paul points out the practical road: flee youthful lusts, follow righteousness, faith, love, and peace, and walk with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart. The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle and patient. Spiritual maturity is not a loud voice but a steady life; not proving yourself right but living out the likeness of Christ.
a: Stay away from fruitless arguments
Do not spend your energy proving yourself.
Study the truth diligently
Let God’s word be the standard for your life.
Live out a gentle life
Treat everyone with patience and love.
q: Am I pursuing proving myself, or pursuing God’s approval?
pr: Heavenly Father, guard my mouth and my heart so that I do not fall into fruitless arguments. Make me a worker who has no need to be ashamed, one who rightly receives and lives out Your truth. Give me the gentleness and patience of Christ, to the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be a worker who has no need to be ashamed, faithfully holding to the truth and living out the gentleness and patience of Christ.

t: What Are You Sowing?
v: Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that will he also reap.
For he who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.
Let us not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let’s do what is good toward all men, and especially toward those who are of the household of the faith.
b: This passage reveals a law of life: sowing and reaping. God has set a spiritual principle: whatever a person sows, that will he also reap. Today’s thoughts, choices, habits, and words are all seeds. People may ignore this, but God’s law does not change. It may not show in the short term, but in the long term it will surely be clear.

Paul sets two kinds of sowing before us: sowing to the flesh, or sowing to the Spirit. Sowing to the flesh means letting the old self be king, living by selfish desire, temper, and self-centeredness, and in the end reaping corruption. Sowing to the Spirit means letting Jesus be King and obeying God’s leading, and in the end reaping life and peace.

So Paul encourages us: “Let us not be weary in doing good.” Many people lose heart because they do not see a harvest right after sowing. But God’s timing is never wrong, and in due season there will be a harvest. Loving others, serving faithfully, and obeying quietly may seem silent, but all of it is sprouting beneath the soil. Do not lose heart; keep sowing the right seed.
a: Examine your daily sowing
What are my thoughts and actions planting?
Choose to sow to the Spirit
Let the Lord lead, rather than letting emotions and desires rule.
Keep doing good without losing heart
Believe that God will bring the harvest in his time.
q: Is the pattern of my recent life sowing to the flesh, or sowing to the Spirit?
pr: Heavenly Father, shine Your light on me so that I see what I am sowing each day. Help me refuse the way of the flesh and choose to walk by the Spirit. When I am weary, give me patience and hope, so that I do not lose heart until I see Your harvest. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I sow to the Spirit and do not lose heart in doing good. In due season I will reap.

t: What Kind of Soil Is Your Heart?
v: When a great multitude came together, and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable.
“The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and brought forth fruit one hundred times.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
“Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
Those along the road are those who hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
That which fell among the thorns, these are they who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.
That in the good ground, these are they who in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it fast, and bring forth fruit with patience.”
b: This passage tells us that the problem is not the seed, because the seed is the word of God. The problem is the soil, the human heart. God’s word itself has life and power, but if the heart is closed and hardened, like the soil along the road, the word cannot get in and is quickly taken away.

Some hearts are like rocky ground. They receive the word with joy at first, but have no root. If faith stays at the level of feeling and is not rooted in truth, it falls back when testing comes. Other hearts are like thorny ground, choked by cares, riches, and pleasures. They did hear the word, but too many other things have filled the field of the heart.

The key to good soil is “an honest and good heart” and “bringing forth fruit with patience”: being willing to let God shine his light, being willing to obey, and persevering. Bearing fruit in life is not done in a day, but is the result of holding on over time. When people receive God’s word wholeheartedly and let Jesus be King, they will bear a hundredfold fruit of life.
a: Check the condition of your heart
Is my heart hard, shallow, or crowded with other things?
Let truth take root every day
Not just being moved, but continually reading, obeying, and practicing.
Wait patiently for the fruit
Hold fast to God’s word, and life will surely mature.
q: Which soil does my heart most resemble right now? What do I need God to clear away?
pr: Heavenly Father, prepare the soil of my heart and remove its hardness, shallowness, and thorns. Let Your word take deep root in me, so that I hold fast to the truth and bear fruit with patience. May my life become good soil that glorifies Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My heart is good soil. God’s word takes root and grows in me, and I bear a hundredfold fruit.

t: Seeing the Creator Leads to Worship
v: Bless Yahweh, my soul. Yahweh, my God, you are very great. You are clothed with honor and majesty.
He covers himself with light as with a garment. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain.
He lays the beams of his rooms in the waters. He makes the clouds his chariot. He walks on the wings of the wind.
He makes his messengers winds, and his servants flames of fire.
He laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be moved forever.
You covered it with the deep as with a cloak. The waters stood above the mountains.
At your rebuke they fled. At the voice of your thunder they hurried away.
He sends springs into the valleys. They run among the mountains.
They give drink to every animal of the field. The wild donkeys quench their thirst.
The birds of the sky nest by them. They sing among the branches.
He waters the hills from his rooms. The earth is filled with the fruit of your works.
He causes the grass to grow for the livestock, and plants for man to cultivate, that he may bring out food from the earth,
and wine that makes glad the heart of man, oil to make his face to shine, and bread that strengthens man’s heart.
Yahweh’s trees are well watered, the cedars of Lebanon, which he has planted,
Let Yahweh’s glory endure forever. Let Yahweh rejoice in his works.
He looks at the earth, and it trembles. He touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to Yahweh as long as I live. I will sing praise to my God while I have any being.
b: This psalm leads us to see the Creator through creation. Sky, earth, wind, water, and mountains all proclaim God’s greatness. He is not a distant God, but the Lord who governs and sustains all things. When people see God’s greatness, awe and praise naturally arise in the heart.

God not only created, he also continues to provide. Springs flow, plants grow, food nourishes people, and all creatures are satisfied, showing that he is a Father who cares for every detail. He watches over the wild animals and the birds, and he watches over our needs too. Often we see only what we lack, and forget that each day’s provision comes from God’s gracious hand.

So the psalmist ends with a response: “I will sing to Yahweh as long as I live.” True worship is not only singing in a gathering. It is a lifestyle that arises from seeing God. When our focus is on Jesus, not on ourselves and our circumstances, complaining turns to thanksgiving and anxiety turns to praise.
a: Think of God through his creation
Every day, see God’s work through nature and daily life.
Count your everyday provisions
Give thanks for God’s care in the small things.
Live a life of worship
Respond to God’s grace with thanksgiving and praise.
q: Lately, have I been seeing more of my problems, or more of God’s wonderful provision?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are the Lord who created heaven and earth and provides for all things. Open my eyes so that I see Your work in my daily life. Let me stop complaining, and respond to You with thanksgiving and worship all my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I see God’s greatness and provision, and all my life I will bless Yahweh.

t: Hearing the Lord’s Voice, Entering Abundant Life
v: “Most certainly, I tell you, he who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.
But he who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out.
When he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him, for they don’t know the voice of strangers.”
Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them.
Jesus therefore said to them again, “Most certainly, I tell you, I am the sheep’s door.
All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep didn’t listen to them.
I am the door. If anyone enters in through me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out, and will find pasture.
The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.”
b: This passage shows us that Jesus is the good shepherd and also the door of the sheep. He does not force the sheep to follow; he calls them by name and goes ahead to lead them. The Lord knows each one of us. We are not a number in a crowd, but precious lives known personally and called personally by him.

Jesus says the sheep know the shepherd’s voice. The world has many voices: anxious voices, accusing voices, tempting voices, the voice of self. But the Lord’s sheep learn to tell the Lord’s voice apart. The Lord’s voice brings peace, truth, direction, and life. As we draw close to the Lord, we come to know his leading more and more.

Jesus also declares, “I am the door.” True safety, salvation, and provision are all in him. The thief comes to steal, kill, and destroy, but the Lord came that we may have life, and have it abundantly. Abundant life is not having more things. It is letting Jesus be King and living in his presence and guidance.
a: Listen for the Lord’s voice every day
Through prayer and the Bible, grow sensitive to telling his voice apart.
Refuse the voice of strangers
Do not follow fear, temptation, and accusation.
Go in and out through the Lord
Go to Jesus first in everything and let him lead.
q: Lately, which voice do I listen to most, the world’s or the Lord’s?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that through Jesus You are my shepherd and the door of the sheep. Make me sensitive to Your voice, so that I do not follow the voice of strangers. Lead me on Your path every day, so that I experience the abundant life You give. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I know the Lord’s voice and follow his leading. In Christ I have abundant life.

t: Whom You Trust Shapes Who You Become
v: Yahweh says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart departs from Yahweh.
For he will be like a shrub in the desert, and will not see when good comes, but will inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land which is not inhabited.
Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh.

For he will be like a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green, and will not be concerned in the year of drought, neither will it cease from yielding fruit.”
b: This passage divides life into two roads: trusting in people, or trusting in God. To trust in the arm of flesh means to build our hope on human ability, relationships, money, status, and our own cleverness. It may look solid outside, but inside it easily loses its foundation, because people are limited and circumstances change.

God describes such a person as a shrub in the desert, living in a parched land, not seeing good when it comes. It is not that God does not bless, but that when life is cut off from its source, even blessing is hard to receive. When the heart departs from Yahweh, a person grows more dry, anxious, and unsettled inside.

But blessed is the one who trusts in Yahweh. This person is like a tree planted by the waters, with roots spread out by the river. When heat comes, there is no fear; in a year of drought, the tree still bears fruit. Circumstances may be hard, but life is supplied. True stability is not the absence of storms, but having roots in God. When Jesus is King, life can stay green and keep bearing fruit.
a: Examine what you lean on
What is my sense of security really built on?
Return to the source every day
Let prayer and God’s word water your life again.
Trust the Lord in your circumstances
Even in heat and drought, believe God will provide.
q: When pressure comes, is my first reaction to rely on myself, on people, or on the Lord?
pr: Heavenly Father, search my heart and remove my wrong dependence on people and on myself. Help me to rely on You alone, so that I am like a tree planted by the waters, rooted in Your love and truth. Whatever my circumstances, let me stay green and bear fruit, to the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I rely on Yahweh alone. I am like a tree planted by the waters, and in every season I will not cease to bear fruit.

t: Today, Do Not Harden Your Heart
v: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice,
don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion, like as in the day of the trial in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me and tried me, and saw my deeds for forty years.
Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways;’
as I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter into my rest.’”
Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there be in any one of you an evil, unbelieving heart, in falling away from the living God;
but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today;” lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end,
while it is said, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”
b: This passage keeps repeating one phrase: “Today if you will hear his voice.” The moment when God works is often today, not tomorrow. Many people know the truth but keep putting off obedience; they know they should turn back but say, “later.” God reminds us that the best time to respond to him is today.

The Israelites saw God’s works for forty years in the wilderness, yet still hardened their hearts. The problem was not a lack of miracles, but unbelief in the heart. When people look only at circumstances and not at God, they easily complain, go astray, and lose rest. What truly blocks people is not the wilderness outside, but the hardness inside.

So the text says to exhort one another day by day, lest we be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin. Spiritual life needs reminders and companions; do not try to bear it alone. When we hold the beginning of our confidence firm and let Jesus continue to be King, we can enter the rest and abundance found in Christ.
a: Respond to God today
Do not delay obedience; act now.
Keep your heart from hardening
When you meet a reminder, choose to be humble and teachable.
Walk with spiritual companions
Encourage one another and watch over one another.
q: Is there something God has recently said to me that I have known but not yet obeyed?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me a soft heart, so that when I hear Your voice today I respond at once. Save me from unbelief and hardness, and give me spiritual companions to support one another. Let me hold fast to my first confidence and enter the rest You have prepared. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Today I listen to the Lord’s word. My heart is soft and obedient, and I hold my confidence firm to the end and enter the Lord’s rest.

t: With God’s Presence, You Can Prosper Anywhere
v: Yahweh was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. He was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
His master saw that Yahweh was with him, and that Yahweh made all that he did prosper in his hand.
Joseph found favor in his sight. He served him, and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, Yahweh blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. Yahweh’s blessing was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
He left all that he had in Joseph’s hand. He didn’t concern himself with anything, except for the food which he ate. Joseph was well-built and handsome.
Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound; and he was there in custody.
But Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.
The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Yahweh was with him; and that which he did, Yahweh made it prosper.
b: This passage repeats one phrase: “Yahweh was with Joseph.” Joseph was not blessed in an ideal environment. He was sold as a slave and wrongly thrown into prison. But God’s presence turned the land of slavery into a land of blessing, and turned the prison into a place of preparation.

The world often defines success as high status, good circumstances, and no difficulties; but in the Bible, to prosper is to have God with you. Joseph was faithful in his master’s house and faithful in prison. His outward position changed, but his inner life did not. A truly prosperous person is defined not by where he stands, but by whether God is with him.

Joseph did not become bitter over being wronged, and did not give up in the low place. In every place he let God be in charge, so wherever he went he brought blessing. When people let Jesus be King, even if they are temporarily in a low place, God can still make them a blessing to others, and lift them up at the right time.
a: Value God’s presence above circumstances
First ask for the Lord to be with you, not only for circumstances to change.
Be faithful in small places
Wherever you are, do your duty wholeheartedly.
Reject bitterness and complaining
Believe that the low places are also God’s preparation.
q: Do I care more about whether my circumstances are going well, or about whether God is with me?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are with me as You were with Joseph. When I am in a difficult environment, give me faithfulness and faith. Keep me from complaining and from losing heart, so that in every place I live out Your glory and become a channel of blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God is with me, and I will prosper wherever I am. I will be a vessel of blessing.

t: Zeal Is Not Enough; We Must Follow God’s Way
v: David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
The anger of Yahweh was kindled against Uzza, and he struck him, because he put his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.
David was displeased, because Yahweh had broken out against Uzza; and he called that place Perez Uzza, to this day.
David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?”
So David didn’t move the ark home to himself, into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
b: This passage begins with lively worship: singing, dancing, and joy, all seeming spiritual and zealous. Yet things suddenly came to a halt, because Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark and was struck down. This reminds us that zeal itself is not obedience. A person can be very zealous in doing God’s work without doing it in God’s way.

The problem was not the ark, and not the worship, but that they had not carried the ark in the order God had commanded. When people replace God’s way with their own, it is easy to think, “I mean well.” Uzza’s reaching out may have come from a wish to help, but God values obedience, not human self-direction.

David was afraid of God because of this, and learned reverence again. Spiritual maturity is not only loving God but also fearing him; not only serving with zeal but also obeying the truth. The focus is not how I want to do it, but what the Lord says. To let Jesus be King is to lay down my own ideas and walk in his will.
a: Seek understanding before zeal
Before doing the Lord’s work, seek the Lord’s heart.
Do not replace truth with your own ideas
Good intentions apart from obedience can still go wrong.
Restore a heart of reverence
Honor the Lord as great and do everything according to God’s word.
q: When I serve God, am I acting more out of enthusiasm, or according to God’s truth and leading?
pr: Heavenly Father, forgive me for sometimes being zealous yet acting in my own way. Give me a teachable heart, so that I not only love You but also fear You. Let me seek Your will in everything and walk according to Your truth. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not serve God by my own ideas. I fear the Lord and walk in truth in God’s way.

t: In Babylon, Do Not Forget Zion
v: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept when we remembered Zion.
On the willows in its midst, we hung up our harps.
For there those who led us captive asked us for songs. Those who tormented us demanded songs of joy: “Sing us one of the songs of Zion.”
How can we sing Yahweh’s song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill.
Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I don’t remember you, if I don’t prefer Jerusalem above my chief joy.
b: This psalm expresses the pain of a people in exile. They were in Babylon, but their hearts longed for Zion; their bodies were in a foreign land, but their spirits still thirsted for God’s presence. Babylon stands for the worldly system that exalts self and moves away from God; Zion stands for God’s dwelling and his Kingdom. When people leave the center of God, they may be alive outwardly, but often feel loss inside.

They hung their harps on the willows because in their suffering they could not sing. This reminds us that sometimes our lives also enter a valley, where worship seems silent and joy seems lost. Yet even as they wept, they did not forget Zion. The real danger is not tears, but forgetting God.

The psalmist declares, “If I forget you…” This is a resolve: even when living in Babylon, do not let the heart become Babylon. Today we also live in the world, but our focus must remain on Jesus. Our circumstances may be in Babylon, but our hearts should dwell in Zion; we are on earth, but our hearts are toward the Kingdom of heaven.
a: Discern Babylon’s influence
Watch whether the world’s values are stealing your longing for God.
Remember the Lord even in the valley
Even while weeping, do not stop drawing near to God.
Let your heart dwell in Zion
In a busy world, hold on to a heavenly focus.
q: Have I lately been so busy that my heart is slowly forgetting its longing for God?
pr: Heavenly Father, as I live under the pressures of the world, keep my heart from being shaped by Babylon. Even when I pass through a valley, let me not forget You or lose my longing for Your presence. Help me fix my eyes on Jesus every day and keep my heart in Your Kingdom. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Though I live in the world, my heart belongs to God. I will not forget Zion, and I fix my eyes on Jesus to the very end.

t: God Can Turn the Wilderness into Springs
v: “The poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue fails for thirst. I, Yahweh, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the midst of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree. I will set in the desert the cypress, the plane tree, and the pine together;
that they may see, and know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of Yahweh has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.”
b: This passage first describes the people’s plight: poor and needy, seeking water and finding none, their tongues failing for thirst. This is not only outward lack; it is also like the inner thirst, weariness, and helplessness of the heart. Often it is only at the end of ourselves that we discover what we truly need is not more resources, but God himself.

Yet God declares, “I will answer them… I will not forsake them.” When people have no way out, God still has a way. He can open rivers on the bare heights and springs in the valleys, turn the wilderness into a pool and dry land into springs. The end of people is often the beginning of God’s work; the driest place may be exactly where grace is about to flow.

God does not only meet a temporary need; he brings renewal and growth. He plants trees in the wilderness and sets them in the desert, so that people may see that the hand of Yahweh has done this. When Jesus is King, a barren life can flourish again, and a place of despair can grow hope. God loves to turn the impossible into a testimony.
a: Admit your thirst
Bring your real needs before God.
Believe God can still make a way
Even if circumstances are like a desert, expect God’s springs.
Notice what God does
Record how God shows grace in barren places.
q: Which area of my life is like a wilderness? Do I believe God can open springs there?
pr: Heavenly Father, when I am weary and thirsty, thank You that You have not forsaken me. Open rivers in my wilderness and bring springs up from the dry ground. Renew my withered heart so that my life may grow and bear fruit again, a testimony that glorifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God does not forsake me. He will turn my wilderness into springs and make life grow in barren ground.

t: When We Turn to the Lord, the Veil Is Taken Away
v: But if the service of death, written and engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, which was passing away,
won’t service of the Spirit be even more with glory?
For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.
But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
b: This passage tells us that true glory is not in outward religious form but in the life found in Christ. The old covenant law had glory, but it could only point out human sin; what Jesus brings is righteousness, forgiveness, and new life, a glory that is greater and lasting. God does not only want people to keep rules; he wants them to be renewed.

Paul says there is a veil over the heart. The veil stands for hardness, blind spots, self-centeredness, and spiritual covering. A person may read the Bible for years and still not see the Lord, or do many things without understanding God’s heart. The problem is not that God is not speaking, but that the heart is veiled.

But there is a precious promise: “Whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.” When people humbly turn to Jesus, the Holy Spirit brings freedom and change. It is not by our own self-effort, but by fixing our eyes on the glory of the Lord that we are gradually transformed into his image. True growth is from glory to glory, becoming more and more like Jesus.
a: Turn to the Lord every day
Turn your attention from yourself and circumstances to Jesus.
Ask the Lord to take away the veil
Ask the Holy Spirit to shine on your blind spots and hardness.
Be changed by fixing your eyes on the Lord
Through worship, prayer, and Bible reading, let your life be renewed.
q: Is there a veil in my life that keeps me from seeing God’s will clearly?
pr: Heavenly Father, turn my heart to You and remove every covering and hardness. Let me find freedom in the Holy Spirit and see the glory of the Lord every day. May I no longer live in the old self, but go from glory to glory, becoming more and more like Jesus. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My heart turns to the Lord, and the veil is taken away. The Holy Spirit sets me free, and I will go from glory to glory, becoming like Jesus.

t: You Are Not an Orphan; the Holy Spirit Lives in You
v: the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive; for it doesn’t see him, neither knows him. You know him, for he lives with you, and will be in you.
I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.
In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
One who has my commandments, and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?”
Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our home with him.
He who doesn’t love me doesn’t keep my words. The word which you hear is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me.
“I have said these things to you while still living with you.
But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.
b: This passage is full of comfort. Jesus knew his disciples would face anxiety and separation, so he promised to send the Holy Spirit. He said, “I will not leave you orphans.” Believers may once have felt loneliness among people, but spiritually you have never been an orphan, because God himself lives with you.

Jesus says the Spirit of truth “lives with you, and will be in you.” This is not merely outward help but an indwelling presence. The Holy Spirit within us comforts, reminds, enlightens, and guides. When we are helpless, he is the Counselor; when we are confused, he is the Spirit of truth.

The Lord also points out that those who love him will keep his word. Obedience is not trading for love; it is the response of love. When we are willing to let Jesus be King and follow his word, we experience more deeply God’s making his home with us and revealing himself to us. The greatest blessing in life is not that everything goes smoothly, but that God lives in us.
a: Reject the orphan mindset
Remember that you are not abandoned, but a child of God.
Learn to depend on the Holy Spirit
Seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance in all things great and small.
Respond to the Lord’s love with obedience
Put the truth you know into practice.
q: Lately, am I living in loneliness and anxiety, or in the assurance of the Holy Spirit’s presence?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You have not left me an orphan but have sent the Holy Spirit to live in me. Make me sensitive to the Spirit’s voice, so that every day I receive comfort and guidance. Help me love You and obey You, and experience more of the grace of Your making Your home with me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am not an orphan. The Holy Spirit lives in me. God dwells with me, and I am led every day.

t: Losing the Throne, but Not Losing God
v: All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.

Behold, Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
The king said to Zadok, “Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I will find favor in the eyes of Yahweh, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation.
But if he says thus, ‘I have no delight in you;’ behold, here am I, let him do to me what seems good to him.”
The king said also to Zadok the priest, “Aren’t you a seer? Return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem; and they lived there.

David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered and went barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
One told David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” David said, “Yahweh, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.”
b: This passage records the low point of David’s life. His son Absalom rebelled, the people wept, and the king was forced to leave Jerusalem. Outwardly David seemed to have lost everything: throne, city, security, honor. But in the darkest hour he still held on to one thing, God’s sovereignty.

David did not treat the ark as a lucky charm, nor use religion to score points for himself. He said, “If I find favor in the eyes of Yahweh, he will bring me again; if he has no delight in me, let him do to me what seems good to him.” This is deep surrender. True faith is not manipulating God to accomplish our wishes, but entrusting ourselves to God’s will.

David went up the Mount of Olives weeping, and yet he prayed. His tears did not stop his faith, and his pain did not stop him from seeking God. Spiritual maturity is not never weeping, but looking to the Lord even while weeping. A person may lose a position but must not lose God; circumstances may shake, yet the heart can remain at peace in the Lord.
a: Acknowledge God’s rule even in trouble
Do not look only at what you have lost; see that God is still on the throne.
Let go of control and learn to surrender
Entrust the outcome to God’s will.
Keep praying even while weeping
Come to the Lord with your honest emotions.
q: When I lose something important, do I blame God, or surrender to him more deeply?
pr: Heavenly Father, when I go through loss and upheaval, make me trust You as David did. Help me not to cling to outward position, but to hold on to Your presence alone. Let me keep praying even through tears, and acknowledge Your rule even in the low places. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Though I pass through storms, I do not lose God. The Lord reigns, and my heart is at peace.

t: Is Your Mouth Building Up or Tearing Down?
v: An evil man is snared by the transgression of his lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.
A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. What a man’s hands have done shall be rendered to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
He who breathes out truth shows righteousness, but a false witness, deceit.
There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only for a moment.
Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the counselors of peace.
No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked shall be filled with trouble.
Lying lips are an abomination to Yahweh, but those who do the truth are his delight.
A prudent man keeps knowledge to himself, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.
b: This passage reminds us that the tongue holds enormous power. We are satisfied with good by the fruit of our mouths. In other words, our mouths are no small matter; they shape our relationships, our direction, and the outcome of our lives. Many blessings begin with one word that builds someone up, and many wounds begin with one impulsive word.

Proverbs says, “There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.” Words can be like a sword that pierces the heart, or like medicine that brings healing. When we live in the old self, the mouth becomes a tool for venting. When Christ lives within us, the mouth becomes a channel of blessing.

The passage also shows that the wise listen to counsel and the prudent overlook an insult. A truly mature person does not take pleasure in sharp words, but has a teachable heart and a disciplined mouth. Someone who lets Jesus be King does not need to win every argument; he only needs every word to glorify God.
a: Think before you speak
Ask: will these words build someone up or hurt them?
Bring healing with your mouth
Offer more encouragement, more thanks, more blessing.
Learn to be quiet and teachable
Don’t rush to argue; be willing to listen to counsel.
q: Lately, have my words been like a sword that pierces, or like medicine that heals?
pr: Heavenly Father, please govern my tongue and cleanse my thoughts. Let me speak honest words, gracious words, and words that build others up. Help me not to speak from my flesh, but let Jesus reign within me, so that my mouth becomes a vessel of blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My mouth belongs to the Lord. I speak words of wisdom, words of peace, and words that heal.

t: To Live Is Christ
v: What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed. I rejoice in this, yes, and will rejoice.
For I know that this will turn out to my salvation, through your supplication and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
according to my earnest expectation and hope, that I will in no way be disappointed, but with all boldness, as always, now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
b: This passage reveals the height of Paul’s life. Some people preached the gospel with impure motives, but Paul did not fix his eyes on them; he fixed them on whether Christ was being made known. When our focus is on ourselves, we are easily hurt, angered, and caught up in comparison. When our focus is on Jesus, we can rise above people’s problems and still rejoice.

Paul was in prison, yet he said that through the prayers of many and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, this would turn out to his salvation. Outwardly he was restricted, but inwardly he was full of freedom. True strength is not smooth circumstances; it is the presence of the Holy Spirit. When a person lets the Lord be King, even chains cannot bind the soul.

The most striking words are these: “For to me to live is Christ.” Paul’s purpose in life was no longer his own success, comfort, or recognition, but that Christ be magnified. This is the life of selflessness: it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. When we live for the Lord, even death loses its terror, for to die is to be with the Lord, which is far better.
a: Adjust your focus in life
Look less at what people are doing, and more at whether Christ is glorified.
Rely on the Holy Spirit in your circumstances
Keep trusting that the Lord can help you in hard times.
Live for the Lord
Each day ask: how can I magnify Christ today?
q: What do I care about most in my life right now: myself, or Christ being magnified in me?
pr: Heavenly Father, please change the focus of my life so that I no longer center on myself. Let me be like Paul, rejoicing in every circumstance and strengthened by the Holy Spirit. May my living be Christ, and may Jesus be lifted high in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: To me, to live is Christ. My life will make Jesus great.

t: When You Return, God Remembers His Covenant
v: “‘If they confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, in their trespass which they trespassed against me, and also that, because they walked contrary to me,
I also walked contrary to them, and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and they accept the punishment of their iniquity;
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

The land also will be left by them, and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will accept the punishment of their iniquity, because they rejected my ordinances, and their soul abhorred my statutes.
Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break my covenant with them; for I am Yahweh their God.
But for their sake I will remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am Yahweh.’”
b: This passage shows us the heart of God. Even when his people rebelled and went their own way, God still prepared a door for them to return. The first step is not running away, but confessing our sin. True revival often begins with humility; true healing often begins with facing ourselves honestly.

God specifically speaks of an “uncircumcised heart” being humbled. Outward religious behavior cannot replace inward change. The problem is often not our circumstances, but a heart set against God. When a heart softens and is willing to yield, God’s grace begins to flow. Humility overcomes pride, and returning opens the door to restoration.

The most moving words are these: God says, “I will not reject them... and break my covenant with them.” Human unfaithfulness cannot cancel God’s faithfulness. You may have wandered far, but God has not forgotten his covenant. When a person turns to the Lord, he still opens his arms to receive them. God’s discipline has a purpose: to bring his people home.
a: Come honestly before God
Don’t justify your mistakes; truthfully admit your need of the Lord.
Practice humility of heart
Lay down pride and resistance, and learn to submit to God.
Hold on to God’s faithfulness
Even when you fall, trust that God has not given up on you.
q: Is there an area of my life where I need to confess, return, and surrender to God again?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are a God who keeps covenant and shows steadfast love. When I drift away, please shine Your light on me, so that I will be willing to confess my sin and return to You with a humble heart. Thank You for not rejecting me and not abandoning Your promises. Restore me, so that I may walk in Your ways again. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I humbly return to the Lord. God remembers his covenant, and he will restore me.

t: Those Who Wait for the Lord Will Not Be Disappointed
v: Hear, Yahweh, when I cry aloud. Have mercy also on me, and answer me.
When you said, “Seek my face,” my heart said to you, “I will seek your face, Yahweh.”
Don’t hide your face from me. Don’t put your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Don’t abandon me, neither forsake me, God of my salvation.
When my father and my mother forsake me, then Yahweh will take me in.
Teach me your way, Yahweh. Lead me in a straight path, because of my enemies.
Don’t deliver me over to the desire of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen up against me, such as breathe out cruelty.
I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.
Wait for Yahweh. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for Yahweh.
b: This passage shows us that even under pressure and attack, David chose to seek God’s face. He did not first ask for his circumstances to change; he first asked for God’s presence. True peace is not the instant disappearance of problems, but being able to draw near to the Lord in the middle of the storm.

David said, “When my father and my mother forsake me, then Yahweh will take me in.” These are deeply comforting words. People may disappoint you and relationships may break, but God never abandons those who belong to him. When the world closes a door, God still opens one; when people do not accept you, God still takes you in.

At the end David speaks to himself: “Wait for Yahweh.” Waiting is not passive delay; it is standing in faith, believing that God is at work. Often not seeing the answer is the hardest thing, yet it is what trains our faith best. Without trust in God’s goodness we easily lose heart; but believing in God’s timing, we can take courage and be strengthened.
a: Seek God’s face first
When something happens, draw near to the Lord first, instead of being carried away by emotions.
Believe God never forsakes you
Even when people fail you, God remains faithful.
Practice waiting on the Lord
Hold on to faith before you see the answer.
q: What do I need most right now: an immediate answer, or to return to God and wait on him?
pr: Heavenly Father, when my heart is anxious, draw me to seek Your face first. When people let me down, help me remember that You will take me in. Give me strength to wait, so that even before I see the answer, I may take courage and trust Your goodness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will wait for the Lord. My heart will be strengthened, and I will see the Lord’s goodness.

t: Don’t Give the Devil a Foothold
v: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor. For we are members of one another.
“Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath,
and don’t give place to the devil.
Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labor, producing with his hands something good, that he may have something to give to him who has need.
Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice.
And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
b: This passage reminds us that spiritual warfare often begins in the details of daily life. The devil does not always attack with a great storm; very often he gains ground slowly through lies, anger, bitterness, and harsh words. When we let our emotions run free, cling to our own way, and refuse to forgive, we leave an opening for darkness.

Paul says, “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Anger itself is an emotion and is not necessarily sin; but if we hold on to wrath until the sun goes down and let it ferment, it easily turns into harm. Many relationships are not ruined by big events, but by accumulated resentment and unhealed wounds. If we do not give it to the Lord, anger becomes the enemy’s tool.

God also gives us a path of renewal: speak the truth, work and share, speak words that build up, be kind, and forgive one another. This is the shape of the new self. When Jesus is King, the mouth no longer wounds, the heart no longer harbors bitterness, the hands are no longer selfish, and relationships begin to be healed. Don’t give the devil a foothold; give the Holy Spirit room to reign.
a: Deal with anger right away
Bring it to God and don’t let the emotion stay overnight.
Build people up with your words
Deliberately speak encouragement, comfort, and blessing today.
Choose to forgive and release
Hand your bitterness to the Lord and give the enemy no place to stay.
q: Where in my life am I giving the devil a foothold?
pr: Heavenly Father, please shine Your light on the hidden anger, bitterness, and dark openings in my heart. Forgive me for letting my emotions rule and not letting You be King. Holy Spirit, cleanse me, so that I may speak true and edifying words, live out kindness and forgiveness, and have my life governed by You again. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I give the devil no foothold. I let the Holy Spirit reign, and I live in forgiveness and freedom.

t: Healing Often Begins with Humility and Obedience
v: Now Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and highly honorable, because by him Yahweh had given victory to Syria. He was also a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
The Syrians had gone out in bands, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maiden. She waited on Naaman’s wife.
She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”
So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariots, and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean.”

But Naaman was angry, and went away, and said, “Behold, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’

His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean?’”
Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
b: Naaman looked honored and successful on the outside. He was a mighty warrior and a commander, yet inside he had a leprosy he could not solve. This reminds us that a person can have status, ability, and achievement, and still have a break deep in life. The world can cover outward problems, but only God can heal the inner ones.

When Elisha gave a simple instruction, Naaman became angry, because God’s way did not match his expectations. He wanted a spectacular miracle, but received a lesson in humble obedience. Often people don’t fail to receive help; they simply cannot let go of themselves. Pride makes us resist simple truth, while humility opens the door of grace.

When Naaman humbled himself and went down to the Jordan seven times, he was made clean, and his flesh was like that of a child. God often heals the heart first, then the circumstances. True renewal often begins with obedience. When we lay down our own ideas and let Jesus be King, life can be restored as new.
a: Admit your need
Don’t just keep up appearances; come honestly before the Lord.
Let go of your own ideas
Accept God’s way and don’t insist on your own.
Respond to God with obedience
Even when the method is simple, be willing to do as he says.
q: Have I missed the healing and change God wants to give me because of pride and stubbornness?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for seeing the real need behind my outward success. Please remove my pride, so that I am willing to humbly obey Your leading. Whatever You say, I am willing to do. Heal the depths of my life and make me clean and new. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I lay down my pride and humbly obey the Lord. God will heal and renew me, and my life will be made new.

t: Giving Is Not Only Giving Away, but Learning to Fear God
v: You shall eat before Yahweh your God, in the place which he chooses to cause his name to dwell, the tithe of your grain, of your new wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock; that you may learn to fear Yahweh your God always.
If the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the place is too far from you, which Yahweh your God chooses to set his name there, when Yahweh your God blesses you;
then you shall turn it into money, and bind up the money in your hand, and shall go to the place which Yahweh your God chooses.

You shall spend the money for whatever your soul desires: for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatever your soul asks of you; and you shall eat there before Yahweh your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.
You shall not forsake the Levite who is within your gates; for he has no portion nor inheritance with you.
At the end of every three years, you shall bring out all the tithe of your increase in the same year, and shall lay it up within your gates.

The Levite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, and the foreigner, and the fatherless, and the widow, who are within your gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hand which you do.
b: This passage shows us that giving is not merely a matter of money; it is a lesson in fearing God. God wanted his people to bring the tithe before him so they would remember that every provision comes from God. If we only enjoy the blessing and forget the Lord who blesses, our hearts slowly drift from him.

God also let his people eat and rejoice in his presence. This reminds us that worship is not a burden, but joy together with God. True giving is not loss, but entering a deeper connection. When we are willing to give our best to God, we learn not to be ruled by money, but to let Jesus be King.

Finally, the passage specifically mentions the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows. God cares for the weak and the needy. Those who truly fear God not only give to God, but also share with others. When blessing stops with ourselves, it easily turns into selfishness; but when blessing flows outward, it becomes a channel of God’s grace.
a: Fear God through giving
Remember that everything is given by God.
Rejoice before God
Treat worship as a time of joy together with the Lord.
Learn to share the blessing
Care for those in need and become a channel of provision.
q: Is my attitude toward money one of clinging tightly, or of entrusting it to God’s care?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being the source of all my provision. Help me not to rely on possessions, but to fear You and trust You. Make me a willing giver and a joyful sharer, so that my life becomes a blessing to others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God is the source of all provision. I give willingly and share the blessing joyfully.

t: Don’t Stay Where You Are; Press On Toward Christ
v: So then, my beloved, even as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.
Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect; but I press on, if it is so that I may take hold of that for which also I was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before,
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, think this way. If in anything you think otherwise, God will also reveal that to you.
Nevertheless, to the extent that we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule. Let us be of the same mind.
b: Although God used Paul greatly, he still said, “I am not already made perfect.” A truly mature person does not feel he is already good enough, but keeps longing to become more like Christ. If we stop pursuing in our spiritual life, we easily stagnate, become complacent, and even slowly fall back.

Paul said, “Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before.” Many are bound by the past: some live in failure, some live in former glory. But God wants us to keep moving forward. Whether yesterday brought success or a fall, don’t stay where you are, but run straight toward God’s goal.

This passage also reminds us that real change does not come from gritting our teeth on our own, but from God working within us. When a person is willing to obey, the Holy Spirit gives strength, prompting, and direction. To work out our salvation is not to trade works for salvation, but to let salvation be truly lived out in our lives, showing the likeness of Christ.
a: Don’t stay in the past
Let go of yesterday and keep moving forward.
Pursue becoming more like Jesus every day
Keep being renewed in your thoughts, words, and actions.
Obey the Holy Spirit’s leading
Believe that God is at work in you.
q: Am I stuck in the past right now, no longer pressing on toward Christ?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for not giving up on shaping me. Help me neither to grow complacent nor to lose heart, but to pursue becoming more like Jesus every day. Let me forget what is behind and press on to what is ahead, obeying the Holy Spirit’s work in me and living out Your good purpose. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not stay where I am. I run straight toward Christ, and God is accomplishing his good pleasure in me.

t: A Person with God’s Presence Brings Peace
v: Now the Spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from Yahweh troubled him.
Saul’s servants said to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God troubles you.

Let our lord now command your servants, who are before you, to seek out a man who is a skillful player on the harp. It will happen, when the evil spirit from God is on you, that he will play with his hand, and you will be well.”
Saul said to his servants, “Provide me now a man who can play well, and bring him to me.”

Then one of the young men answered, “Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a handsome person; and Yahweh is with him.”
So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said, “Send me David your son, who is with the sheep.”
Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a container of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by David his son to Saul.
David came to Saul, and stood before him. He loved him greatly, and he became his armor bearer.
Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my sight.”
When the evil spirit from God was on Saul, David took the harp, and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
b: This passage shows us that what truly brings a person peace is not musical skill alone, but the presence of God. David was praised not only because he could play the harp, but, more importantly, because “Yahweh is with him.” A person who has God’s presence within brings out heavenly peace and comfort.

Saul was still king outwardly, but inwardly he was full of torment. David was only a shepherd boy outwardly, but inwardly he had the Spirit of God. The world values position and appearance, but God values the life within. What truly influences people is not status, but what fills you on the inside.

When David played the harp, Saul was refreshed and well. This reminds us that God wants us to become people who bring peace. When Jesus lives within us, wherever we go we can carry grace, comfort, and healing. Life matters more than skill, and presence matters more than ability.
