a: Pursue God’s presence
Don’t seek only power; seek closeness with the Lord even more.
Become someone who brings peace
Spread the peace of Christ at home, in church, and at work.
Serve God with your gifts
Make the talents God has given you a tool to bless others.
q: When others come near me, do they sense pressure, or peace that comes from God?
pr: Heavenly Father, make me like David, with Your presence within me. Let me pursue not only outward ability, but inward life. Use my gifts and my words to make me someone who brings peace and comfort. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God is with me. I will be a vessel of peace and comfort.

t: Living in the Light Is Living in Love
v: This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie and don’t tell the truth.
But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard.
Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away, and the true light already shines.
He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness even until now.
He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him.
b: This passage declares an important truth: “God is light.” Light represents holiness, truth, and life; darkness represents sin, self, and hiding. A person who truly walks with God will not keep living in darkness. Spiritual life is not an outward religious appearance, but truly walking in the light.

Walking in the light does not mean never making mistakes; it means being willing to face our sin honestly. The most dangerous thing is not weakness, but pretending we have no problem. When we are willing to confess and no longer hide, the blood of Jesus cleanses us from all unrighteousness. Light exposes, but it also heals.

John then points out the mark of truly living in the light: loving our brothers and sisters. If a person says with his mouth that he loves God but his heart is full of bitterness, hatred, and rejection, he is actually still living in darkness. Love is not a feeling, but a life. When Jesus lives within us, the darkness gradually passes away and the true light begins to shine.
a: Live honestly before God
Don’t hide your weakness; truthfully confess your sin to the Lord.
Stay away from dark thoughts
Refuse bitterness, jealousy, and hatred.
Live out the light with love
Take the initiative to forgive, accept, and care for others.
q: Is there hidden darkness in my life, or unforgiveness toward someone?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are the true light and in You is no darkness. Please shine on my heart so that I do not live in hiding and self-deception. Cleanse me with the precious blood of Jesus, and put love within me, so that I may live in the light and live out a life of loving one another. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I live in God’s light. The precious blood of Jesus cleanses me, and I will live out the light with love.

t: Even in the Deepest Place, God Hears Your Prayer
v: Then Jonah prayed to Yahweh his God out of the fish’s belly.
He said, “I called because of my affliction to Yahweh, and he answered me. Out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice.
For you threw me into the depths, in the heart of the seas. The flood was all around me. All your waves and your billows passed over me.
I said, ‘I have been banished from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head.
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth with its bars closed behind me forever; yet have you brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh my God.
“When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahweh. My prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
“Those who regard worthless vanities forsake their own mercy.
But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah onto the dry land.
b: Jonah ran from God and ended up in the storm and the belly of a fish. But the darkest place became the place where he prayed again. Often people drift from God when things go well, but remember the Lord in the low valley. The fish’s belly seemed like a prison, yet it became Jonah’s prayer room of returning.

Jonah said, “When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahweh.” Only when a person reaches the end does he discover that true rescue is not in himself, but in God. Jonah was wrapped in weeds and surrounded by the deep, yet God still heard his cry. No abyss is deeper than God’s grace, and no low point is greater than God’s mercy.

In the end Jonah declared, “Salvation belongs to Yahweh.” True deliverance is not through human methods, but through God’s grace. When a person is willing to turn to the Lord, God can turn the fish’s belly into a new beginning. Falling is not the end; returning is the key.
a: Turn to God in the low valley
Don’t run from the Lord; come back before him.
Keep praying in despair
Believe God still hears your cry.
Acknowledge that salvation belongs to God
Lay down self-reliance and trust in the Lord alone.
q: Am I in the “belly of the fish” in my life right now? Am I willing to turn to God again?
pr: Heavenly Father, when I fall into low and dark places, thank You that You still hear my cry. Forgive me for running from You and drifting away. Bring my heart back before You, so that even in hardship I keep looking to You. I declare: salvation belongs to the Lord. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Even in the deepest valley, God hears my prayer. Salvation belongs to the Lord.

t: With the Lord Present, You Lack Nothing
v: A Psalm by David. Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
He restores my soul. He guides me in paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
b: This psalm does not say there will be no valleys in life; it says that even when we pass through the valley, a shepherd walks with us. David did not say, “I will not pass through the shadow of death.” He said, “I will fear no evil,” because God was with him. True peace is not the absence of storms, but knowing that the Lord is holding you in the storm.

That the Lord is a shepherd means he is not only a provider but also a guide. Sheep don’t know the road ahead, but the shepherd does. Often our greatest problem is not a lack of answers, but an unwillingness to be led. When we let Jesus be King, we can move from anxiety into rest, and from self-reliance into being shepherded.

At the end David declares, “Goodness and loving kindness shall follow me.” Not occasionally, but all the days of my life. God’s love is not a passing emotion, but a continuing companionship. Even when circumstances change, God’s grace does not leave. The truly blessed are not those who have much, but those who have the Lord’s presence in their lives.
a: Entrust the control of your life to the Lord
Learn to let Jesus be the shepherd of your life.
Trust in the valley
Don’t look only at circumstances; remember the Lord is with you.
Live in gratitude every day
Believe that goodness and loving kindness are following you.
q: Am I leading myself right now, or am I truly letting the Lord be my shepherd?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being my good shepherd. When I am weary, You make me rest; when I am lost, You guide me; when I walk through the valley, You are still with me. Help me no longer rely on myself, but follow You with a settled heart, living all my days in Your goodness and loving kindness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. The Lord is with me, and my heart is at rest.

t: True Love Walks Together and Never Lets Go
v: Naomi said, “Go back, my daughters. Why will you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
Go back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons,
would you wait until they were grown? Would you refrain from having husbands for them? No, my daughters, for it grieves me much for your sakes, for Yahweh’s hand has gone out against me.”
They lifted up their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
She said, “Behold, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law.”
Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Yahweh do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”
When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
b: This passage is full of tears and parting. Naomi had lost her husband and her sons, and felt her life was without hope; she even believed God had struck her. She urged her two daughters-in-law to leave, because she could no longer give them a future. But in that very darkest moment, Ruth chose to stay.

Ruth’s love was not built on advantage, but on commitment. She did not leave because circumstances were hard; she chose to walk together in the most difficult time. She said, “Your people will be my people, and your God my God.” True love is not only companionship in good times, but never letting go in the low valley.

Ruth’s decision also changed her whole life. She went from being a foreign widow to entering God’s plan of redemption, and even became part of the genealogy of Jesus. Often we think we are simply being faithful, not knowing that God is preparing greater grace behind the scenes. When we are willing to walk together in love, God can turn suffering into blessing.
a: Stay faithful in hardship
Don’t love people only in good times.
Learn never to let go
Live out commitment in your family, with companions, and in the church.
Choose God’s way
Like Ruth, recognize God as the Lord of your life.
q: When others are in a low and weak place, do I choose to leave, or am I willing to walk with them?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me a faithful love like Ruth’s, so that I love not only those who are easy to love but am willing to stay with those in the low valley. Help me learn commitment and walking together, and let me, in the choices of my life, recognize You as my God. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk together with faithfulness and love. I recognize the Lord as my God, to the very end.

t: True Abundance Is Being Content in Any Situation
v: But I rejoice in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your thought for me; in which you did surely take thought, but you lacked opportunity.
Not that I speak in respect to lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
I know how to be abased, and I also know how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
However you did well that you shared in my affliction.
You yourselves also know, you Philippians, that in the beginning of the Good News, when I departed from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only.
For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need.
Not that I seek for the gift, but I seek for the fruit that increases to your account.
But I have all things, and abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things that came from you, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
b: Paul said, “I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.” This is not a natural personality; it is something he “learned.” Contentment does not come from perfect circumstances, but from having the Lord within. The world makes us feel that “a little more and I’ll be happy,” but true peace is not having more; it is knowing that God is enough.

Paul had experienced being abased and abounding, being filled and being hungry, yet he discovered a secret: “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” True strength does not come from holding on by ourselves, but from Christ. When we let Jesus be our satisfaction, we are no longer controlled by circumstances.

Paul also thanked the church in Philippi for their provision, calling it a sacrifice pleasing to God. Giving is not only an exchange of money, but a flow of love and faith. When we are willing to be a provider for others, God will also supply us according to his riches in glory. God’s Kingdom is not a cycle of lack, but a cycle of grace.
a: Learn to be content in the present
Don’t let comparison and greed steal your peace.
Rely on Christ for strength every day
Don’t just hold on by yourself; depend on the Lord’s strength.
Be glad to be a provider
Help others with love, giving, and action.
q: Is my joy right now built on my circumstances, or on the Lord?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being my true satisfaction. Teach me to learn contentment in every situation, not bound by lack or comparison. Let me depend on You for strength every day, and gladly be a channel of blessing to others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Christ is my satisfaction. I draw strength from the Lord, and I can be content in any situation.

t: Pride Brings a Fall; Humility Draws Us Near to God
v: How you are fallen from heaven, day-star, son of the morning! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!
You said in your heart, ‘I will ascend into heaven. I will exalt my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north.
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds. I will make myself like the Most High.’
Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
b: This passage shows us that the root of Satan’s fall was not a lack of ability, but pride. He was once a bright star, but he fell because of “I will.” The essence of pride is leaving one’s rightful place and wanting to take God’s throne. When a created being no longer worships God but wants to exalt himself, he begins to walk toward darkness.

In the passage the words “I will ascend” and “I will make myself like the Most High” appear again and again. This is the heart of humanity’s fall: unwilling to obey God and wanting only to live by our own will. When a person lives in self-centeredness, he easily exalts himself, grasps for power, and tries to prove himself, and in the end drifts farther and farther from God.

But God’s way is exactly the opposite. Jesus, though in the form of God, emptied himself and took a humble heart. Satan fell because he exalted himself; Jesus was lifted high because he humbled himself. True victory is not lifting ourselves up, but letting Jesus be King. Humility is not thinking little of ourselves; it is returning to our rightful place as human beings and letting God be God.
a: Notice the “I will” in your heart
Do you often want to control, prove, or exalt yourself?
Practice humble obedience
Learn to lay down your own will and let the Lord reign.
Fix your eyes on Jesus’ example
Imitate Christ’s self-emptying and self-giving.
q: Is there a place in my life where I want to exalt myself and take the place of God’s sovereignty?
pr: Heavenly Father, please shine Your light on the pride and self-exaltation within me. Forgive me for trying to be king by myself and not letting You reign. Give me a humble heart, and bring me back to my rightful place as a human being, so that I lift up Jesus alone. May I live my whole life in obedience, not in self. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I choose humility and obedience. I do not exalt myself; I let Jesus alone be King.

t: God Will Make All Things New
v: I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more.
I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God.
He will wipe away from them every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.”
He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
b: This passage is one of the most hope-filled pictures in the Bible. God does not merely patch up the old world; he will bring “a new heaven and a new earth.” Today the world still has tears, death, pain, and brokenness, but none of it is forever. God has already prepared a fully renewed Kingdom.

The most precious words are these: “God himself will be with them.” The greatest blessing for humanity is not only going to heaven, but dwelling with God forever. From the Garden of Eden on, God has longed to walk with people; sin separated us from God, but the salvation of Jesus has opened the way of his presence again. The very heart of the glory of God’s Kingdom is God himself.

God also declares, “Behold, I make all things new.” This is not only a future promise; it is a work that begins today. When a person lets Jesus be King, God begins to renew the heart, renew relationships, and renew life. Past pain is not the end; God can make the wasteland bloom again and turn failure into a new beginning.
a: Live with an eternal perspective
Don’t look only at temporary troubles; remember the future glory of God’s Kingdom.
Believe God can renew your life
No matter how broken, God can restore it.
Long for God’s presence
True heaven is dwelling with the Lord forever.
q: What do I long for most right now: the satisfactions of this world, or God’s presence forever?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing a new heaven and a new earth for us. As I live in a world full of pain and brokenness, let me still be full of hope. Thank You for promising to wipe away every tear and to make all things new. May I long for Your presence every day and live in eternal hope. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God is renewing me. I live in eternal hope, and I will dwell with the Lord forever.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Suffer for Righteousness
v: Who is he who will harm you, if you become imitators of that which is good?
But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t be afraid of their threats, neither be troubled.”
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts; and always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear:
having a good conscience; that, while you are spoken against as evildoers, those who curse your good manner of life in Christ may be put to shame.
For it is better, if the will of God is so, that you suffer for doing well than for doing evil.
b: Peter reminds believers that those who follow Jesus will not always be understood by the world. Sometimes, because of your honesty, kindness, and holding to the truth, you may be misunderstood, shut out, or even made to suffer. But God says, “Even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed.” Such a life is living out the likeness of Christ.

The passage does not tell us to live in fear; it says, “Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts.” When Jesus is truly King, we no longer fear people’s opinions excessively. Often people compromise because they care too much how others see them; but when our focus returns to Jesus, we can stand firm under pressure.

Peter also teaches us to answer people “with meekness and fear.” Truth is not for winning arguments against others, but for living out Christ. The most powerful witness is not only speaking well, but keeping goodness and a clear conscience even when wronged. Such a life is itself the gospel.
a: Don’t compromise the truth under pressure
Even when you are not understood, choose to do good.
Let Jesus be King in your heart
Don’t be ruled by people’s opinions.
Witness with gentleness
Share the gospel through your life, not only your words.
q: What do I fear most right now: people’s opinions, or losing my faithfulness to the Lord?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me a heart of courage and gentleness, so that even under pressure I am willing to hold fast to the truth. When I am misunderstood or wronged, help me not to panic, but to honor the Lord as holy. May my life become a witness that glorifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not fear people’s opinions. I honor Christ the Lord as holy, and I will live out the truth with my life.

t: While You Were Still Weak, God Loved You First
v: For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a righteous person someone would even dare to die.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
b: This passage shows us that God’s love is not because we deserve it, but because he gave it freely. People often feel, “Once I get a little better, then God will love me.” But the Bible says Christ died for us while we were still weak, while we were still sinners.

The world’s love is often built on conditions: you are loved if you have value, accepted if you perform well. But God’s love is not an exchange; it is grace. Jesus did not wait until we were perfect to save us; he reached out his hand first, when we were at our most failing, our darkest, and our most helpless. The greatest proof of the cross is that God loved us first.

A person who truly understands this love is changed. When we know we are accepted unconditionally, we no longer need to prove our worth by performance. The selfless life no longer lives in self-blame and condemnation, but in the love of Christ. It is not how good I am, but how great God’s grace is.
a: Receive God’s love
Don’t draw away from God because of your weakness.
Don’t trade performance for love
Understand that grace is not earned.
Respond to others with love
Take the initiative to love, as Christ did.
q: Do I still feel I must perform well enough to be worthy of God’s love?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for loving me while I was still weak and still a sinner. Please remove the inferiority, condemnation, and feelings of unworthiness within me, so that I truly believe Your grace. Teach me also to love others with the same love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am not loved because of my performance. I am accepted and saved by the grace of Christ.

t: True Service Is Willing to Pay the Price for Love
v: Are they servants of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself.) I am more so: in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in deaths often.
Five times I received from the Jews forty stripes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I have been a night and a day in the deep.

I have been in journeys often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers;
in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.
Besides those things that are outside, there is that which presses on me daily, the care of all the assemblies.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I don’t burn with indignation?
b: Here Paul does not boast of success, but tells of his scars. His real authority did not come from position, but from the price he paid for Christ. Today the world likes to look at outward glamour, but God values inward faithfulness.

Paul experienced beatings, prison, danger, hunger, and persecution, yet did not give up. He did not live for himself, but for Christ and for people’s souls. True love always carries sacrifice; true service also requires self-giving. If we only want comfort, it is hard to truly carry the weight of lives.

The most moving words are these: “Who is weak, and I am not weak?” His heart was not only in the work, but in the people. This is the heart of Christ. It is not using people to get the work done, but being willing to weep for them, care for them, and pay the price for them. Life matters more than tasks, and relationships matter more than results.
a: Don’t avoid the cost
Be willing to pay the price for truth and love.
Shepherd people with love
Care about people’s lives more than the results of tasks.
Persevere by the Lord’s strength
Even when it is hard, don’t leave God’s calling.
q: Is my service for building myself up, or truly for the love of God and others?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for showing me through Paul the shape of true service. Give me a faithful and loving heart, so that I pursue not only outward results but am willing to pay the price for people’s lives. When I am weary and weak, add to my strength, so that I may keep faithfully following You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am willing to be faithful to Christ to the end, to serve people with love, and to live out a life of self-giving.

t: Rise Up and Build; No More Desolation
v: Then I said to them, “You see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we won’t be a reproach any more.”

I told them of the hand of my God which was good on me, and also of the king’s words that he had spoken to me. They said, “Let us rise up and build.” So they strengthened their hands for the good work.
Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate. They laid its beams, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, repaired that which belonged to the throne of the governor beyond the River.
Next to him Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths, repaired. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired, and they fortified Jerusalem to the Broad Wall.
Next to them Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
Next to them Jedaiah the son of Harumaph repaired opposite his house. Next to him Hattush the son of Hashabneiah repaired.
Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hasshub the son of Pahath-moab, repaired another section, and the tower of the furnaces.
Next to him Shallum the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.
b: When Nehemiah saw Jerusalem lying waste, he did not merely sigh; he rose up to build. People who truly belong to God do not only see the problem; they are willing to become the answer. Many only criticize the fallen wall, but Nehemiah chose to respond to God’s prompting: “Come, let us build!”

The most beautiful part is that the building was not done by one person, but by everyone taking part together. There were officials, goldsmiths, perfumers, and even daughters. Each person repaired his own section. God’s Kingdom is not built by a few heroes, but by everyone who is willing to offer himself, working together in unity.

Today God is also looking for people willing to “rise up and build.” Perhaps it is building a family, a church, a relationship, a life. Desolation does not restore itself; someone must be willing to respond to God. When we lay down the attitude of a bystander and begin faithfully building our own section, God’s glory will slowly be restored.
a: Don’t only see the problem
Be willing to become someone who brings restoration.
Faithfully build your own section
Start with your family, small group, and service.
Work together in unity with the body
Build God’s divine order together.
q: Which section of the wall does God want me to rise up and build now?
pr: Heavenly Father, remove from me the heart that only watches and criticizes, and let me be like Nehemiah, willing to rise up and build even when I see desolation. Help me faithfully complete the section You have entrusted to me, and build Your Kingdom together in unity with my brothers and sisters. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will rise up and build. I will faithfully complete the section of the wall God has entrusted to me.

t: True Abundance Is Becoming a Channel of Blessing
v: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
Let each person give as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.
As it is written, “He has scattered abroad. He has given to the poor. His righteousness remains forever.”
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;
you being enriched in everything to all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us.
For this service that you perform not only supplies the needs of the saints, but also abounds through many givers of thanks to God.
Seeing that through the proof given by this service they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the Good News of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all,
while they also, with supplication on your behalf, yearn for you because of the exceeding grace of God in you.
Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!
b: Paul uses sowing to describe giving and generosity. A farmer who never sows will never harvest; in the same way, a person who always clenches his fist will find it hard to experience God’s abundant provision. There is a spiritual principle in God’s Kingdom: sow little, reap little; sow much, reap much.

But what God values more than the amount is the heart. The passage says, “God loves a cheerful giver.” God does not want forced giving; he wants willing love. True giving is not loss but trust; not pressure but worship. When a person is willing to let go, it proves he believes that God is the true provider.

God blesses us not only so that we ourselves may be rich, but so that we may be “generous.” God’s true abundance does not stop with us; it flows out to become a blessing to others. When love flows, thanksgiving goes up to God, and his glory is revealed.
a: Sow in faith
Believe that God is the source of all supply.
Give willingly and cheerfully
Not under compulsion, but out of love for God.
Become a channel of blessing
Let God’s grace flow through you to others.
q: Is my attitude toward money and resources one of clinging tightly, or of being willing to become a channel of blessing?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being a God who gives grace generously. Please take away the sense of lack and the fear within me, so that I learn to sow in faith and to give and share willingly and cheerfully. May my life not only receive blessing but also become a blessing to others, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God is my provider; I sow willingly, and I will be a channel through which blessing flows.

t: Walking the Highway of Holiness, You Will Never Be Lost Again
v: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Way of Holiness. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way; even if they are fools, they will not go astray.
No lion will be there, nor will any ravenous animal go up on it. They will not be found there; but the redeemed will walk there.
The ransomed of Yahweh will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
b: God promises his people a “Highway of Holiness.” This road is not the world’s road; it is a road set apart as holy, leading back to God. The world’s road looks wide but often leaves people lost; God’s road requires obedience, yet it brings true peace and life.

The passage says, “Even if they are fools, they will not go astray.” What a comfort! Those who follow God do not walk the right path because they are clever, but because God himself leads them. Many times we do not know the way ahead, but as long as we fix our eyes on Jesus and obey the Holy Spirit, we will never truly be lost.

In the end God paints a picture of glory: the redeemed return rejoicing, and sorrow and sighing flee away. This is not only the hope of the Kingdom to come; it is a life that begins today. When a person leaves the darkness and returns to God’s presence, the burdens within begin to be released, and true joy returns.
a: Choose to walk God’s road
Do not follow the world’s values, but follow the truth.
Fix your eyes on Jesus and you will not be lost
Even when you cannot see what lies ahead, trust that the Lord is leading.
Live in the joy of redemption
Do not remain long in sorrow and sighing.
q: On the road I am walking now, am I drawing closer to God, or drifting further from him?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing a holy highway for me. When I am weak and confused, please guide me personally so that I do not stray from Your way. Let me fix my eyes on Jesus every day, walk in the light, and live in the joy of Your redemption. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk on God’s highway of holiness; the Lord will guide me, and I will never be lost again.

t: When the Heart Turns to God, Even the Night Becomes Morning
v: “Can you fathom the mysteries of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
They are high as heaven. What can you do? Deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
For he knows deceitful men. He sees iniquity, even when he does not consider it.
An empty-headed man becomes wise when a wild donkey’s colt is born a man.”
“If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
Surely then you will lift up your face without spot. Yes, you will be steadfast and will not fear;
for you will forget your misery. You will remember it as waters that have passed away.
Your life will be clearer than noonday; though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.
You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search around you, and will take your rest in safety.
Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope is a dying gasp.”
b: This passage reminds us that God’s wisdom is far beyond human understanding. When people meet suffering, they are quick to ask, “Why?” But finite human beings cannot fully fathom the Almighty. When we rely only on our own reasoning, we easily fall into complaint and confusion; but when we learn to revere God, we can still trust him even when we do not understand.

The passage specifically says, “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.” The real key is not only whether the outward problem is solved, but whether the heart within has turned back to God. When a person is willing to put away sin and unrighteousness and let Jesus be King again, life begins to be restored to light and peace.

God promises, “Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.” This is a great hope. God can turn a person’s night into dawn and make pain like waters that have passed away. Perhaps today you are still in a low valley, but as long as your heart turns to the Lord, hope will not go out. True rest is not an easy set of circumstances, but God’s presence within once again.
a: Do not rely only on your own understanding
Learn to revere God and trust his wisdom.
Set your heart aright again
Put away the sin and unrighteousness in your life.
Hold on to hope in the darkness
Believe that God can turn night into morning.
q: Am I relying on my own understanding right now, or have I truly turned my heart to God?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being the all-powerful and all-knowing God. When I do not understand the path of my life, please help me not to lean on my own cleverness but to learn to trust You. Cleanse my heart and turn me back to You, and let Your light shine again on my dark night. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I trust in God’s wisdom; my night will become morning, and in the Lord I have hope and rest.

t: Those Who Dwell in God Have True Security
v: Because you have made Yahweh your refuge, and the Most High your dwelling place,
no evil shall happen to you, neither shall any plague come near your dwelling.
For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone.
You will tread on the lion and cobra. You will trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot.
“Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him. I will set him on high, because he has known my name.
He will call on me, and I will answer him. I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him, and honor him.
I will satisfy him with long life, and show him my salvation.”
b: This passage is not a guarantee that life will never have storms. It declares that those who truly make God their dwelling place are protected in the storm. The world’s security is built on money, position, and ability, all of which can be shaken; only God is a refuge that never changes.

God specifically says, “Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him.” True protection is not only outward peace but an inward connection. When a person loves the Lord wholeheartedly and trusts him, he lives under God’s covering. Even in times of distress, he does not face them alone, because God says, “I will be with him.”

The passage also speaks of “trampling the lion and the serpent,” which represents overcoming the enemy and the powers of darkness through God. Christians do not win by their own courage, but because God is with them. When Jesus is King, fear no longer rules us, because we know that God is greater than our circumstances.
a: Make God your true dwelling place
Do not lean on him now and then, but live in the Lord every day.
Call on God first in trouble
Do not rely only on your own methods.
Love and trust the Lord wholeheartedly
Let your heart live under God’s covering.
q: Is my true security built on the world, or on God?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being my refuge and my dwelling place. When I face the unknown and danger, take away my fear, and help me to love You and trust You wholeheartedly. Thank You for promising to be with me, to protect me, to deliver me, and to show me Your salvation. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Yahweh is my refuge; I love the Lord wholeheartedly, and I live in God’s protection and presence.

t: True Wisdom Is Trusting God with All Your Heart
v: My son, don’t forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments:
for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
b: This passage is God’s most precious reminder for life: do not rely only on your own cleverness. People’s greatest problem is often not a lack of ability, but trusting themselves too much. When people live only by analysis, experience, and feeling, they easily walk into their own way; but true wisdom is to trust in Yahweh with all your heart.

“With all your heart” means total trust, not half on God and half on yourself. Many times a person says with his mouth that he believes in the Lord, yet in reality still holds on to his own methods and control. True faith is being willing, even when we do not understand, to acknowledge God and obey him, believing that his guidance is higher than our own vision.

God also reminds us not to let kindness and truth leave us. True godly wisdom is not only a sharp mind but an upright life. When we live out kindness and truth and also lean on the Lord, we find favor with both God and people. For God cares not only how fast you go, but whether you go the right way.
a: Do not rely only on your own ideas
Seek God’s guidance first in everything.
Acknowledge the Lord in all your ways
Not only in spiritual matters, but entrust every part of life to God.
Live out kindness and truth
Let your life agree with the truth.
q: What do I lean on most right now: my own cleverness, or God’s guidance?
pr: Heavenly Father, forgive me for so often leaning on my own cleverness instead of trusting You with all my heart. Teach me to acknowledge You in everything and to obey Your leading. Write kindness and truth on my heart, so that I may live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I trust in Yahweh with all my heart and do not lean on my own understanding; God will make my paths straight.

t: Walk by the Spirit and You Will Live Out the Life of Christ
v: For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom for gain to the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you aren’t consumed by one another.
But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh.
For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
Now the works of the flesh are obvious, which are: adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness,
idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies,
envyings, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these; of which I forewarn you, even as I also forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit the Kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.
b: This passage shows us that two forces are at war in a Christian’s life: the flesh and the Spirit. The flesh always wants to exalt itself, satisfy selfish desires, and live by emotion and temper; the Spirit leads a person to live out the life of Christ. If we follow the flesh, we easily fall into strife, anger, envy, and confusion; if we follow the Spirit, we bear the fruit of life.

True freedom is not doing whatever we want, but having the power to no longer be ruled by sin. The world thinks indulgence is freedom, but the Bible says it is actually bondage. True freedom is being able to love, to forgive, to exercise self-control, and to live out God’s likeness.

The fruit of the Spirit is not squeezed out by human effort; it is the life that grows naturally as we abide in Christ. When we let Jesus be King every day and obey the Spirit’s leading, we gradually move from self-centeredness to selflessness, from the old self to the new self. Life is changed not by the pressure of the law, but by the work of the Holy Spirit.
a: Choose to obey the Spirit every day
Do not let emotions and selfish desires rule.
Watch for the fruit of your life
Examine whether you are becoming more like Christ.
Serve one another in love
Do not bite and devour one another, but build each other up.
q: Lately, what has been showing in my life: the works of the flesh, or the fruit of the Spirit?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me not to live by the flesh but to walk by the Spirit. When strife, anger, selfishness, and selfish desires rise within me, please deal with my old self through the cross. Let the Holy Spirit bear in me love, joy, peace, and self-control, so that I become more and more like Jesus. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I live by the Spirit, and I will walk by the Spirit; I will live out the fruit of Christ’s life.

t: Not for People to See, but for the Lord to See
v: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
“Honor your father and mother,” which is the first commandment with a promise: “that it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth.”
[Combined with the previous verse.]
You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the training and admonition of the Lord.
Servants, be obedient to those who according to the flesh are your masters, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as to Christ;
not in the way of eyeservice, as men pleasers, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart,
with good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men,
knowing that whatever good thing each one does, he will receive the same again from the Lord, whether he is bound or free.
b: This passage reminds us that faith is not only worship at gatherings; it is also our attitude in daily life. Whether as children, parents, or workers, we are to live out Christ in our relationships. True spirituality is not merely speaking spiritual words, but living out obedience and love at home and at work.

God specifically reminds children to honor their parents, and parents not to provoke their children. Many family problems are not only a matter of communication skills but a matter of life. When people only want to control and make demands, they easily hurt one another; but when Jesus is King, we learn love and respect. When life is right, relationships will be right.

Paul also says, “with good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men.” This is the most important attitude in the workplace and in ministry. Many people lose their passion because of how others treat them, but if we know that the one we truly serve is the Lord, we can turn from “pleasing people” to “pleasing God.” People may not see, but God sees every act of faithfulness.
a: Live out Christ at home
Learn honor, respect, and love.
Don’t do surface work
Do it not for people to see, but for God to see.
Serve willingly and faithfully
Please the Lord in your work and ministry.
q: What do I care about most right now: people’s praise, or God’s pleasure?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me to live out the life of Christ at home, at work, and in ministry. Remove from me the heart that seeks to please people, and let me truly serve You willingly. Renew my relationships, too, so that I learn obedience, respect, and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not work for people to see; I work for the Lord to see. I will serve the Lord willingly and faithfully.

t: True Holiness Is Living a Life Like God’s
v: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.’
“‘Each one of you shall respect his mother and his father. You shall keep my Sabbaths. I am Yahweh your God.’
“‘Don’t turn to idols, nor make molten gods for yourselves. I am Yahweh your God.’
“‘When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.’
“‘It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the next day. If anything remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.’
“‘If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination. It will not be accepted.’
“‘Everyone who eats it will bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the holy thing of Yahweh. That soul shall be cut off from his people.’
“‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.’
“‘You shall not glean your vineyard, neither shall you gather the fallen fruit of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.’”
b: God said to his people, “You shall be holy.” Holiness is not merely outward religious behavior, but a life that is like God’s. This passage is remarkable because, when God speaks of holiness, he speaks not only of worship, but also of honoring parents, keeping the Sabbath, turning away from idols, and caring for the poor. True holiness means letting God rule every part of life.

God does not want people to have a religious exterior with no heart of love for others. That is why he commanded his people not to reap the corners of their fields when harvesting, but to leave them for the poor and the foreigner. This reveals a heart full of compassion. Those who truly belong to God do not only look after themselves; they also care for those in need. Holiness is not coldness; it carries love and justice.

One sentence appears again and again in the passage: “I am Yahweh your God.” The foundation of all obedience comes from our relationship with God. When a person truly reveres God, he does not merely keep rules, but is willing to live a life that pleases him. God calls us to be set apart from the world, not to isolate ourselves from others in pride, but to live out the light and love of Christ.
a: Live out holiness in daily life
Entrust your family, work, and relationships to God.
Care for those in need
Learn to share and show compassion.
Turn away from idols in your life
Let nothing take the place of God.
q: Does my way of life truly reflect God’s holiness and love?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for calling me to be holy. Please change not only my outside but renew my inside. Let me live out Your will in every area of life, learning to love, to show compassion, and to revere You. May my life reflect Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will live out a holy life that belongs to God, and glorify the Lord in love and truth.

t: Those Who Draw Near to God Will Shine
v: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.
When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him.
Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them.
Afterward all the children of Israel came near, and he gave them all that Yahweh had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses was done speaking with them, he put a veil on his face.
But when Moses went in before Yahweh to speak with him, he took the veil off, until he came out; and he came out, and spoke to the children of Israel that which he was commanded.
The children of Israel saw Moses’ face, that the skin of Moses’ face shone; and Moses put the veil on his face again, until he went in to speak with him.
b: Moses’ face shone, not because he worked hard to put on a display, but because he drew near to God. When a person lives for a long time in God’s presence, God’s glory is naturally reflected in his life. True spirituality is not merely increased knowledge, but a life that begins to change, so that people can sense the light of Christ in you.

What is remarkable is that Moses himself “didn’t know” his face was shining. A person who truly belongs to God does not keep exalting himself. If someone is always trying to show how spiritual he is, he may actually lose the true glory. True glory flows out naturally, not through deliberate packaging. When the focus is on Jesus and not on ourselves, we will carry more and more of the fragrance of Christ.

Each time Moses went in before God, he took off the veil. This reminds us that our spiritual life cannot live only on past experiences. Yesterday’s anointing cannot replace today’s relationship with God. Only by coming before God every day can our life continue to be renewed and illuminated.
a: Draw near to God every day
Spend time reading the Word, praying, and being still before the Lord.
Do not exalt yourself
Keep the focus on Jesus, not on human performance.
Live out the radiance of Christ
Let people sense the Lord’s presence through your life.
q: Lately, has my life become more like Christ because I have drawn near to God?
pr: Heavenly Father, draw me to come near to You every day. Do not let me stay with outward religious activities, but truly live in Your presence. May Your light shine on me, make me more and more like Jesus, and let people see Your glory in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will draw near to God every day, and let the light of Christ shine out from my life.

t: With Man This Is Impossible, but with God All Things Are Possible
v: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into the Kingdom of God.”
When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
But Jesus looked at them and said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
b: Jesus was not saying that having money is itself a sin, but pointing out that if a person relies on wealth, it is very hard for him to truly rely on God. The greatest danger of wealth is not only what is possessed outwardly, but the dependence inwardly. When a person’s security, sense of worth, and sense of control are all built on money, he easily loses his simple trust in God.

The disciples were shocked when they heard this, because people at that time thought wealth was a sign of God’s blessing. But Jesus made them understand that salvation does not come from human ability, status, or achievement. No one can enter God’s Kingdom by himself, because the old self always wants to hold on to itself.

But Jesus ended with a word full of hope: “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” What truly changes a person is not human effort but God’s grace. However hardened a person is, God can change him; however hard an idol is to let go of, God can tear it down. When a person is willing to come humbly before the Lord, God can accomplish what people cannot do.
a: Examine what you rely on
Am I really relying on God, or on the world’s kind of security?
Let go of the idols in your life
Do not let money or status take God’s place.
Believe in God’s great power
Do not despair because of your weakness.
q: What is the hardest thing for me to let go of, the thing most likely to take God’s place in my life?
pr: Heavenly Father, shine light on my heart, and let me see whether I rely on the world more than on You. Help me let go of the idols in my life and trust You simply again. Thank You, too, that where people cannot, You can still do wonderful things. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible; I will trust in the Lord alone.
